scenes.tts: The extra leg enlarged the target. Suppose it doubled the support. Could the survivors double too?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Dial With a Ceiling. Bar: normal survivors, about 12,000. Label: hypothetical, support doubled. Prompt: Pause and predict.
scenes.narration: The extra leg enlarged the target. Suppose it doubled the support. Could the survivors double too?

scenes.tts: Twice twelve thousand is twenty-four thousand. But only about twenty thousand were present at the peak.
scenes.caption: Twice 12,000 is 24,000. But only about 20,000 were present at the peak.
scenes.visual: A ghost bar labelled copy rises toward 24,000 and hits a dashed ceiling line at about 20,000, labelled present at the peak.
scenes.narration: Twice 12,000 is 24,000. But only about 20,000 were present at the peak.

scenes.tts: If no new neurons join afterwards, no target can rescue more than that. That is the ceiling.
scenes.visual: The dashed ceiling line is highlighted. Label: ceiling, if no new neurons join after the peak.
scenes.narration: If no new neurons join afterwards, no target can rescue more than that. That is the ceiling.

scenes.tts: And the real rise was well below it. In embryos with vigorously moving grafts, survivors rose by a tenth to over a quarter.
scenes.visual: A third bar, about 13,300 to 15,400, well below the ceiling. Notes: selected graft cases; 1976 percentages applied to 1975 counts, an illustration.
scenes.narration: And the real rise was well below it. In embryos with vigorously moving grafts, survivors rose by a tenth to over a quarter.

scenes.tts: So the target turns a dial. More target, fewer deaths, up to the ceiling.
scenes.visual: A dial icon beside the bars, turned a little. Label: a dial with a ceiling.
scenes.narration: So the target turns a dial. More target, fewer deaths, up to the ceiling.

scenes.tts: Why did it turn so little? The experiment cannot tell. The graft may be only partly innervated.
scenes.visual: The graft's nerves drawn thin and patchy. Label: how much support it gave is unknown.
scenes.narration: Why did it turn so little? The experiment cannot tell. The graft may be only partly innervated.

scenes.tts: Activity at the muscle also matters.
scenes.visual: A muscle icon beside the column. Label: activity at the muscle.
scenes.narration: Activity at the muscle also matters.

scenes.tts: In chick embryos, paralysing the muscle with koo-rah-ree rescues many motor neurons that would otherwise die.
scenes.caption: In chick embryos, paralysing the muscle with curare rescues many motor neurons that would otherwise die.
scenes.visual: A paralysed muscle icon; more dots stay lit in the column. Label: curare.
scenes.narration: In chick embryos, paralysing the muscle with curare rescues many motor neurons that would otherwise die.

scenes.tts: Is every developmental death the target's doing? One test adds cells instead of target.
scenes.visual: Question card: is every death the target's doing?
scenes.narration: Is every developmental death the target's doing? One test adds cells instead of target.

scenes.tts: Derek Southwell and colleagues transplanted precursors of cortical interneurons into host mice, across a two-hundred-fold range of doses.
scenes.caption: Derek Southwell and colleagues transplanted precursors of cortical interneurons into host mice, across a 200-fold range of doses.
scenes.visual: Credit: Southwell and colleagues, 2012. A log-scaled axis labelled cells transplanted, spanning 200-fold.
scenes.narration: Derek Southwell and colleagues transplanted precursors of cortical interneurons into host mice, across a 200-fold range of doses.

scenes.tts: Predict. Take a toy model, where the host can support only a thousand transplanted cells. What fraction dies as the dose rises?
scenes.caption: Predict. Take a toy model, where the host can support only 1,000 transplanted cells. What fraction dies as the dose rises?
scenes.visual: Toy model card: capacity 1,000 cells; illustrative doses 100, 1,000, 5,000, 20,000. Y axis: fraction dying. Prompt: Pause and sketch.
scenes.narration: Predict. Take a toy model, where the host can support only 1,000 transplanted cells. What fraction dies as the dose rises?

scenes.tts: In the toy model, none die until the dose passes a thousand. Then the fraction climbs, to ninety-five percent.
scenes.caption: In the toy model, none die until the dose passes 1,000. Then the fraction climbs, to 95%.
scenes.visual: Toy-model line, labelled hypothetical: 0%, 0%, 80%, 95%, flat and then climbing steeply.
scenes.narration: In the toy model, none die until the dose passes 1,000. Then the fraction climbs, to 95%.

scenes.tts: The real result was different. About the same fraction died at every dose tested.
scenes.visual: A flat band, labelled observed: about the same fraction at every tested dose. Schematic, not data points.
scenes.narration: The real result was different. About the same fraction died at every dose tested.

scenes.tts: And the cells died at their own age, not the host's. They carried their own clock.
scenes.visual: Label: own clock, a separate result. Two age bars, donor and host; the death mark follows the donor bar.
scenes.narration: And the cells died at their own age, not the host's. They carried their own clock.

scenes.tts: Later work showed that, during this window, circuit activity can tune how many survive.
scenes.visual: A second, smaller dial labelled circuit activity appears beside the clock.
scenes.narration: Later work showed that, during this window, circuit activity can tune how many survive.

scenes.tts: The chick has another case, in the neck-level, or cervical, cord.
scenes.visual: Brief cut: chick cervical cord. Credit: Yaginuma and colleagues, 1996.
scenes.narration: The chick has another case, in the neck-level, or cervical, cord.

scenes.tts: Around day four to five, a wave of cervical motor neurons dies, before the later death that follows target contact.
scenes.caption: Around day 4 to 5, a wave of cervical motor neurons dies, before the later death that follows target contact.
scenes.visual: Day counter at days 4 to 5. Some dots in the cervical column fade.
scenes.narration: Around day 4 to 5, a wave of cervical motor neurons dies, before the later death that follows target contact.

scenes.tts: A bigger target did not change this early wave. Nor did paralysis, or the trophic factors tested.
scenes.visual: A larger target, curare and a panel of factors are applied in turn; the early-death count does not change.
scenes.narration: A bigger target did not change this early wave. Nor did paralysis, or the trophic factors tested.

scenes.tts: Drugs that block RNA or protein synthesis reduced it. So it needs new RNA and protein, an active program.
scenes.visual: A synthesis-blocker icon; fewer dots fade. Label: needs new RNA and protein.
scenes.narration: Drugs that block RNA or protein synthesis reduced it. So it needs new RNA and protein, an active program.

scenes.tts: Moved to another level of the cord, the cervical tube still lost its neurons on schedule.
scenes.visual: The cervical tube segment is moved to another level; the same dots fade at the same stage.
scenes.narration: Moved to another level of the cord, the cervical tube still lost its neurons on schedule.

scenes.tts: So, make too many, then let the target keep what it can support.
scenes.visual: Rule card returns.
scenes.narration: So, make too many, then let the target keep what it can support.

scenes.tts: That holds for many peripheral neurons, and for motor neurons at their muscles.
scenes.visual: Three scope tags reappear: survival, not production (chick limb); a dial with a ceiling; not every population.
scenes.narration: That holds for many peripheral neurons, and for motor neurons at their muscles.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: in the limb, the target helps set survival, like a dial with a ceiling. Count across time, and you can see it.
scenes.visual: Closing card: a dial, with a ceiling.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: in the limb, the target helps set survival, like a dial with a ceiling. Count across time, and you can see it.
